I have been working this land for fifty years. I know Quzhou's soil, its dry spells, how the wells hold up in June. At my age, with just my husband and me, I cannot do everything I used to. But I know what this land needs and what I can manage with my own hands and what I hire out for.

My 6.5 mu is split in my head the way it has always been: about 4 mu runs in the wheat-maize rotation, and I keep 2.5 mu for cotton because cotton money comes in separate from grain and I know how to grow it. The picking is harder now but I manage.

For **wheat**, I plant in early October after rotary tilling. I use the improved variety from the county seed station — I stopped saving my own seed about fifteen years ago, the county variety gives better yield. I put down compound fertilizer as base and add urea at jointing. I irrigate three times: once at sowing to get germination, once at jointing, once at heading. Aphids and powdery mildew I spray twice.

For **maize**, right after wheat harvest in June I seed directly into the stubble — no tilling, the county extension people showed us this saves time and moisture. I use hybrid seed, everyone around here does. Maize gets most of its rain in July and August so I only irrigate twice if it's dry. Two pesticide sprays for corn borer and leaf blight.

For **cotton**, I start in late April. Cotton takes more water and more watching than grain. I irrigate four times — boll-setting is the critical moment. I spray six times across the season for bollworm and aphids. The picking I do slowly now, several rounds through September and October.
